newsitem.title: THAILAND: ASIAN EXOTICS - Thai plan fails to spark regionals.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Thai plan fails to spark regionals.

text.p: 0330 GMT - Southeast Asian currencies remain uninspired by Thailand's economic rescue package, as players focus on news of the central bank suspending an additional 42 finance companies.
* Thai baht still weak but selling abates in onshore market while offshore rate shows firmer bias. Baht quoted at 31.70/80 per dollar onshore against 31.70/32.00 late Tuesday.
* Market still awaiting details of size of international aid package for Thailand and lifting of capital controls.
* Malaysian ringgit remains soft after slipping overnight. Seen heading for recent lows as market absorbs news of curbs on swap transactions and remains unimpressed by Malaysia's fundamentals.
* Singapore dollar back below 1.47 level to U.S. dollar as players cover short dollar positions. Downside seen capped near 1.4750 for now.
* Indonesian rupiah firms as short-term rates rise amid tight liquidity. Gains seen capped around 2,580 level as local dollar demand persists.
* Philippine peso edges up as banks sell dollars to abide by central bank's new lower limit on long dollar positions. Peso at 28.54/59 against Tuesday's 28.65 close.
* Taiwan dollar off morning highs despite suspected central bank intervention as U.S. dollar's bullish trend against majors weighs on market.
